verdict_reason: The c-094 outcome correctly restores paging at eight and the inset per the new ruling, but the winning ruling is missing from the conflict's positions and the attribution sentence credits the inset to the wrong ruling.

todos.issue: c-094's outcome now says 'Ruling ian-2026-11-23 ranks first', but c-094's positions array (lines 3196-3232) holds no position from ruling:ian-2026-11-23, and no claim id ruling-ian-2026-11-23-p* exists anywhere in the workarea. Every other ruling that ranks first in a precedence outcome (sam-2026-10-07, sam-2026-10-09, sam-2026-10-09-pm, sam-2026-10-26) appears as a position with a claim. A precedence resolution whose winning source is absent from positions cannot be traced or re-derived; the sam-2026-10-09-pm p1-067 position ('one page per role, no pagination and no inset') is left as the only ruling position, so a re-distil reading positions sees the old answer win - the exact regression the ticket says to prevent.
todos.fix: Must: c-094's positions carry a ruling:ian-2026-11-23 position, with a claim id the source's extract holds, saying the pickers page at eight and the inset returns, so the outcome's winning source is one of its positions. One way: extract the ruling (claims for points 1 and 5), add a position citing them, and keep the outcome as is.

todos.issue: The outcome credits 'ruling ian-2026-11-23 ... on how many a page holds, and ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm on the rest', then lists the restored 'Selected address' inset among the rest. The inset comes back under ruling ian-2026-11-23 point 5 (sources/ruling-ian-2026-11-23.md), and sam-2026-10-09-pm's own position on c-094 says 'no inset'. The attribution sentence contradicts the outcome's own content.
todos.fix: Must: the outcome's attribution names ruling ian-2026-11-23 for both the page size and the inset, and sam-2026-10-09-pm only for the server search and role filtering. One way: 'Ruling ian-2026-11-23 ranks first on how many a page holds and on the inset, and ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm on the rest.'
